credit.credit-words: THE PUBLIC DOMAIN SONG ANTHOLOGY | https://doi.org/10.32881/book2

direction-type.words: One of Foster’s biggest hits, the song was originally published under E.F. Christy’s name and performed by Christy’s Minstrels. Based on parlor songs of the time, W.E.B. DuBois classified it among the sorrow songs he wrote about and W.C. Hand cited it as a song that “touched the heart of Lincoln” and helped make emancipation a reality. However, the original lyrics are controversial today, and the State of Florida worked with the American Music Center at the University of Pittsburgh to create new lyrics to the state song.
